AI has redefined the semiconductor industry. Although companies such as Palantir and CrowdStrike are thriving due to AI, none of their successes would be possible without the advanced chips coming from a few specific companies.

Knowing that, specific semiconductor stocks appear to hold a bright future despite making huge gains in recent years. If you were looking to own four chip stocks for the next decade, you should consider these names.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
Nvidia

The choice of Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) should not come as a surprise. A $1,000 investment at the 1999 IPO would be worth almost $5.7 million today. It earned most of that gain beginning in 2022, when investors discovered the company's chips were powering the advancements of OpenAI's ChatGPT. This set Nvidia up to dominate the AI accelerator niche it created.

What may surprise investors is Nvidia's modest valuation amid its massive gains. Currently, the stock trades at just 29 times earnings, arguably at bargain levels right now. This is despite its stellar performance in the latest quarter, when its $96 billion in revenue increased by 106% yearly. That gain resulted in a net income of almost $60 billion, 126% more than one year ago.

Admittedly, with a $5.6 trillion market cap, Nvidia's future gains may not compare to those in the past. Also, nearly 93% of its revenue comes from the data center segment, which could bring significant pain in an AI bust.

Nonetheless, with its huge growth and relatively low P/E ratio, Nvidia should be on track to continue beating the market for years to come.

Broadcom

Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) is in a similar position to Nvidia. Its specialty chips for corporate clients have gained considerable interest as its customers scramble to improve their AI capabilities. Broadcom has also fostered a software business in recent years, which complements its chip business and could mitigate downside risk should chip sales slow.

That has driven massive gains for its stock over the last few years, and Broadcom's growth phase is unlikely to end soon despite its $1.7 trillion market cap. In the latest quarter, the $29.6 billion in revenue increased by 86% compared to year-ago levels. Also, with only modest cost and expense growth, the $13.1 billion in quarterly net income rose by 216% over the same period.

title: Dan Ives Remains Bullish on Palantir's Stock in 2027 for This Simple Reason
detail:
Dan Ives Remains Bullish on Palantir's Stock in 2027 for This Simple Reason
David Jagielski, CPA, The Motley Fool
Mon, October 12, 2026 at 6:50 AM PDT 3 min read
PLTR
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Dan Ives is a prominent tech analyst, arguably the most popular one out there. He's bullish on the opportunities in artificial intelligence (AI), and one stock that he continues to see lots of potential in is Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR).

Palantir has been delivering impressive results in recent quarters, and its growth has been tremendous. The stock's high valuation has spooked investors, and that was likely a key reason why it was down for much of the year. But since it reported its recent earnings results, it has been surging yet again. And Ives believes that the stock may still rise higher. Here's why.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Ives believes investors are underestimating the near-term growth potential of AI

In a recent post on social media platform X, Ives said that, "investors [are] underestimating the scale and scope of this $4 trillion dollar spending wave." Ives believes that in the coming years, there is still going to be tremendous spending on AI. Due to these opportunities, Palantir was one of the stocks that were his top tech picks for 2027.

Palantir has been a big benefactor of AI-fueled growth, as the company's been winning over customers with its focus on AI sovereignty and the ability for customers to retain control of their underlying data. This is crucial for companies to maintain their competitive advantages and protect intellectual property.

The tech company has been an advocate for that, and it's been a hugely successful strategy. In its most recent quarter, which went up until the end of June, Palantir reported massive 93% revenue growth, which has been accelerating.

Palantir's stock has been soaring of late

In just the past month, Palantir's stock has risen by more than 20%, taking it back to the highs it reached nearly a year ago. The bullishness has seemingly returned, and with Ives taking a favorable view of Palantir for next year, the tech stock may continue to rise higher in the near term.

But while there is plenty of excitement and optimism around Palantir, investors shouldn't overlook its valuation, as it trades at a whopping 180 times its trailing earnings. The business is doing exceptionally well, and its growth rate looks incredible. However, at such a hefty valuation, it could still limit the stock's gains. Plus, it may leave investors vulnerable to a sell-off if market conditions deteriorate, as stocks that are highly valued may have the most room to fall.

Meanwhile, Red Cat Holdings (NASDAQ:RCAT) stock is nearly unchanged at $5.79, a quiet reaction to the debut of its TRICHON drone that contrasts sharply with the rally in Ondas stock. Sector funds are moving in the opposite direction from Ondas stock. Meanwhile, ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) stock is up 3% to $144.39, trailing the gain in Salesforce stock. Notably, Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) stock is down 0.2% to $208.60, lagging both software peers.

The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (CBOE:IGV) is up 0.6%. At the same time, the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 0.2%. Thus, the software segment and Salesforce stock in particular are drawing buyers even as large-cap technology goes practically nowhere.

Bank of America Drops Its AI Disruption Worry

Bank of America raised its price target on Salesforce stock to $285 alongside the upgrade, and the bank sees an AI pivot driving the shares higher. Its reversal rests on the view that large enterprises are unlikely to replace the platforms housing their business logic, data, workflows and compliance frameworks, which counters an earlier concern that AI would disintermediate enterprise software. Barron's headline on the call put it bluntly: "The AI Overhang Is Over, Say Analysts."

The artificial intelligence (AI) frenzy remains intact as the AI infrastructure space remains rock solid, supported by an extremely bullish demand scenario. U.S. stock markets maintained their northward journey in 2026 after an astonishing rally over the past three years. The strong performance was primarily driven by a rejuvenated AI trade.

Here, we have identified three mid-cap AI-infrastructure stocks that are currently trading at more than a 45% discount to their 52-week high prices. Moreover, these stocks have significant price upside potential in the short term.

These stocks are: Innodata Inc. INOD, Calix Inc. CALX and Applied Optoelectronics Inc. AAOI. Each of these stocks currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

The chart below shows the price performance of these three stocks in the past month.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Innodata Inc.

Innodata is benefiting from strong AI data-engineering demand, reusable datasets, high-value pre-training work and expanding opportunities in agentic AI, model evaluation and physical AI. INOD appears to be entering a stronger phase of AI-driven expansion, supported by accelerating customer adoption, improving profitability and a widening set of growth opportunities. The growth story is shifting toward higher-value services.

Growing Structural AI Demand

Innodata specializes in finding, cleaning, prepping, and labeling messy data so that generative, agentic, and physical AI models can mine and model it. Sometimes this even involves creating new synthetic data. Beyond supplying training data, INOD provides reasoning datasets, trust and safety services, model evaluation, agent optimization and physical AI support.

INOD continues to focus on building a stronger delivery framework that supports rising project volume and new customer engagements across major technology clients. By scaling its global operations and enhancing technical delivery, it intends to manage increasing demand for complex data and AI integration projects. It will enable the company to maintain a competitive edge in the fast-evolving AI services market.

One of the most promising aspects of INOD's strategy is its successful customer diversification efforts. On Jan. 29, 2026, INOD entered into a partnership with Palantir Technologies Inc. PLTR to provide data engineering and annotation capabilities to support PLTR's expanding AI platform deployments for event analytics.

Innodata has an expected revenue and earnings growth rate of 42.1% and 28.3%, respectively, for the current year. The stock is currently trading at a 50.4% discount to its 52-week high price.
